title: Agent
rationale: Retain the provenance-agent comparison without equating capabilities, accountability or identity policies. The Riskium Agent category aggregates bearers rather than supplying a new identity principle.
context_interpretation: The explicit AgentKinds set distinguishes human Person from Organization and remains incomplete. Excluding GS-RKM-C047 prevents bearer-kind classification from competing with responsible/authorizing participation. Changed Person/Organization typing rationales are checked at the generalization endpoints.

title: Actor Reference
rationale: Retain the documentary-reference/agent contrast. An actor identifier or description may remain unresolved and is not itself an identified responsible or authorizing agent.
context_interpretation: G-05 inherits InformationArtifact identity; R-53 permits no resolved agent (0..1). The revised documentary rationale does not turn a name, an identifier or local register approval into evidence of an actual mandate.

title: Responsibility Assignment Information
rationale: Retain the claim/relationship contrast. A recorded responsibility assignment can describe an unsupported claim; a provenance association does not supply the full Riskium mandate-grounding contract.
context_interpretation: R-55 links the statement to at most one actual mandate and allows none. R-09 concerns an analytical RiskCase; neither this statement nor missing approval determines that case's existence. A named owner alone does not establish responsibility, accountability and approval authority together.

title: Responsible Agent Role
rationale: Retain an analogy to provenance role/association descriptions. ResponsibleAgentRole is a contextual bearer classification, not a PROV Role function description or the statement recording an assignment.
context_interpretation: The abstract roleMixin inherits no single sortal identity; its person and organization specializations retain their different identities. R-56 supplies a mandatory inherited mediation dependency. This source structure does not prove that a particular mandate actually exists.

title: Authorizing Agent Role
rationale: Retain the bounded analogy. An authorizing role requires a supported authority context; a provenance function or activity participation alone does not establish approval authority.
context_interpretation: The abstract roleMixin aggregates person and organization bearers without supplying identity. R-57 supplies the selected mandatory dependency. Responsible and authorizing participation are not globally exclusive merely because they share Agent as a parent.

title: Responsible Person
rationale: Retain the person/function analogy while preserving the assigned responsible-person role as a contextual participation of the same human bearer.
context_interpretation: G-24 provides the sole inherited identity supplier Person; G-25 supplies the ResponsibleAgentRole path and inherited R-56 mediation. The same human can bear different roles across contexts without being duplicated or merged with an organization.

title: Responsible Organization
rationale: Retain the organization/function analogy without substituting a vocabulary function for a supported responsible-organization participation.
context_interpretation: G-26 preserves the sole Organization identity and G-27 supplies the responsible-role path and inherited R-56 mediation. A corporate representative is not the organization; an organizational record alone is not evidence of a grounded mandate.

title: Authorizing Person
rationale: Retain the analogy while separating human identity from supported approval authority. A provenance role label supplies neither a mandate nor a decision-specific authorization policy.
context_interpretation: G-28 preserves Person identity, G-29 supplies the authorizing-role path and R-57 is inherited. The non-disjoint Person sibling policy permits different contextual roles without asserting that one person fills both distinct participants of one mandate.

title: Authorizing Organization
rationale: Retain the organization/function analogy while treating approval authority as contextual and supported rather than entailed by an organizational name or class membership.
context_interpretation: G-30 preserves Organization identity; G-31 supplies the authorizing-role path and inherited R-57 dependency. Organizational bearer kinds remain distinct from human representatives, while responsible/authorizing participation is not made globally exclusive.

title: Responsibility Role Term
rationale: Retain vocabulary-concept/function context. The controlled term denotes a responsibility or authority kind; selecting the term does not instantiate the actual role or the mandate grounding it.
context_interpretation: The path through ClassificationTerm and VocabularyConcept preserves InformationArtifact identity. R-54 records an assignment's selected term and R-59 a mandate's term; lexical equality alone establishes neither mandate identity nor actual authorization.
